thread.title: UPDATE: Hedge funds are paying a steep price for their love affair with Facebook shares

author: morningstar.com
title: UPDATE: Hedge funds are paying a steep price for their love affair with Facebook shares
text:
By Sue Chang, MarketWatch
Funds combined lost about $6 billion in matter of hours, according to FactSet data
If you think Mark Zuckerberg is the most miserable man on earth this week, the hedge-fund managers who have been bullish on Facebook Inc. as it blasted its way to records might not be too far behind.
Facebook (FB), at least until late Wednesday, was the darling of Wall Street. In survey after survey, the stock won cheers, and the title as the most widely held name among storied investors like David Tepper's Appaloosa and Dan Loeb's Third Point. The stock rode their adulation to dizzying heights to close at a record of $217.50 Wednesday before it all came tumbling down. Neither Appaloosa nor Third Point responded to requests for comments.
Some 200 hedge funds, or roughly 26% of the funds monitored by Goldman Sachs, owned Facebook with an average weighting of 4%, according to a report issued by the investment bank.
Also see:Here are the 20 stocks that the biggest hedge funds love most (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/here-are-the-stocks-that-hedge-funds-love-most-2018-05-17)
"The 19% dive in FB's stock price [Thursday] hurt hedge fund returns and our VIP basket given that it appears most often as a top 10 position across our analyzed universe of U.S. hedge funds with 10 to 200 individual equity positions," said Arjun Menon, a strategist at Goldman Sachs.
Stocks that most frequently appear among the largest 10 holdings of hedge funds
Read: Facebook pays for all its mistakes at once, and it is a big bill (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/facebook-pays-for-all-its-mistakes-at-once-and-it-is-a-big-bill-2018-07-25)
Facebook's meltdown was staggering. The company's shares tanked in Wednesday's extended session, shedding 25% at their worst. Investors continued to punish Facebook on Thursday with the stock losing about $120 billion in market cap and hedge funds seeing their combined holdings drop roughly $6 billion in value, according to FactSet. The decline marked the biggest ever one-day loss (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/how-facebooks-120-billion-loss-ranks-among-the-biggest-one-day-stock-disasters-2018-07-26) in market cap for a company in recent market history.

And it isn't just hedge funds that are suffering. Facebook was also a favorite with exchange-traded funds and can be found as an underlying asset in many large ETFs along with Apple Inc. (AAPL), Amazon.com Inc. (AMZN), Microsoft Corp. (MSFT) and Alphabet Inc. (GOOGL) (GOOGL), JP Morgan Chase & Co. (JPM), data from Blue Edge Capital show.
In contrast, mutual funds have largely escaped unscathed, Menon said, as they tend to be underweight on Facebook.
"Mutual fund allocation to FB and FANG has declined during the past few years. Due to their consistent FANG underweight over time, core funds have delivered the highest median relative returns during the 41 previous episodes (since 2014) when one or more of the FANG stocks fell by 5%+ in one day," he said.
FANG is a an acronym for Facebook, Amazon.com, Netflix Inc. (NFLX), and Alphabet Inc.'s Google -- a quartet of high-growth stocks that has played a pivotal role in the stock market's rally over the past few years.
Still, given Facebook's prominence among hedge funds and institutional investors, the stock's performance will likely have a direct bearing on where the market is headed, since, as Goldman Sachs noted recently, it was responsible for 8% of the S&P 500's returns this year.
As of yet, not everyone is jumping ship.
Heather Bellini, Goldman's Facebook analyst, is maintaining a buy rating on the stock even though she cut her 12-month price target to $205 from $225 on expectations of lower earnings per share.
Shares of Facebook tumbled 19% Thursday, its worst one-day drop on record, to close at $176.26 and extended losses on Friday, dragging on the tech-heavy Nasdaq which is falling for a second day. The S&P 500 is also down while the Dow Jones Industrial Average is struggling to gain a foothold in positive territory.
-Sue Chang; 1130ET
